statement: Tree DP max-weight matching (not greedy matching) is the necessary matching strategy for achieving score 100 on bushy trees: greedy matching uses 3.88n rounds on bushy trees (max_degree ~124) vs DP's 2.02n, exceeding the 3n scoring threshold and causing consistent score degradation to 99.37.
regime: Bushy trees with max_degree > ~50, where multiple type-2 edges compete for the same internal node
mechanism: At high-degree internal tree nodes, multiple type-2 edges (weight=2) compete for the same parent vertex. The tree DP (O(n) bottom-up computation) considers dp0[u] (leave u unmatched for parent) vs dp1[u] (match u with best child), globally optimizing matching weight. Greedy matching scans edges in input order (idx 1 to n-1), often matching a suboptimal edge early and blocking better alternatives at the same node. On bushy trees (test 20, n≈492, max_degree≈124), this produces 92% more rounds (3.88n vs 2.02n), pushing past the 3n scoring threshold. On low-degree trees (paths, random trees), greedy performs comparably or slightly better than DP because conflicts are rare.
applicability_bounds: Applies specifically to bushy tree structures with high-degree internal nodes (degree > ~10). On path graphs and random trees with low max-degree, greedy matching achieves comparable round counts to DP and the score difference vanishes.

statement: The four critical algorithmic components for score 100 are: (1) anti-oscillation via depth-parity coloring (RP-1, without: 5), (2) tree DP max-weight matching (RP-6, without: 99.37), (3) array-based adjacency (RP-3-refined, without: 96), (4) DFS timestamp routing (RP-4, equivalent to BFS but more timing-robust). Removing any of components 1-3 causes measurable score degradation; the severity decreases by component: 95pts, 0.63pts, 4pts respectively.
regime: Tree matching sort on n≤1000 with 1-second time limit and scoring formula s=(10n-m)/(7n)
mechanism: Three-iteration ablation study systematically removed each component: iter-1 removed anti-oscillation (score 100→5, period-2 oscillation prevents convergence), iter-2 removed array adjacency (score 100→96, cache misses in per-round DP loop cause TLE), iter-3 removed tree DP matching (score 100→99.37, greedy exceeds 3n rounds on bushy trees). DFS timestamps (iter-2) are equivalent to BFS in correctness but use O(n) vs O(n²) precomputation, providing timing headroom.
applicability_bounds: This hierarchy is specific to the scoring formula (10n base, 3n best) and n≤1000 test sizes. For larger n or tighter time limits, the relative importance of components may shift.
